answer:
ANÁLISIS COMPLETO EJECUTADO (script: analysis/urban_invasion_analysis.py; log completo: analysis/results.txt; 103 líneas de salida). Paquetes usados finalmente: pandas 3.0.2, numpy 2.4.4, scipy 1.16.0, statsmodels 0.14.6 (sin herramientas filogenéticas: Bio/ete3/dendropy no disponibles → familia/género como agrupación, según autorizó).

HIPÓTESIS (respuesta en lenguaje natural):
"Urban land use promotes the invasion of introduced plants mainly by filtering which plant types establish: invasion occurrence rises steeply with urbanization (presence of invaders goes from 8.6% of parcels in the lowest urban-cover tercile to 65.2% in the highest at 500 m), but this is largely mediated by habitat type — urban-habitat plots are invaded in 83% of cases vs <7% in forests/scrublands/rock outcrops (habitat is the dominant predictor, LRT chi2=91, p~1e-15). Within invaded plots, urbanization shifts the invading flora's composition: species introduced unintentionally (annual herbs with the broadest invaded niches) increase their share (54%→67% of invaders from low to high urban tercile), while AgriForest introductions almost disappear (8%→2%, p=0.017) and gardening-introduced woody species decline (38%→32%; conditional Poisson IRR for gardening = 0.43, p=0.043). Thus urban land use favors unintentionally introduced, ruderal annual species over deliberately introduced ornamental/agricultural ones; species success overall is best predicted by unintentional pathway (+9.7 invaded plots vs gardening, p=0.009), broader invaded niche breadth (Kruskal-Wallis p=0.047) and longer residence time (log mrt p=0.03), and the modern flora is increasingly gardening-sourced (75% of 1985-2019 introductions vs 17% before 1500), meaning the urban filter acts on an ever-growing ornamental pool."

EVIDENCIA CLAVE (cifras del log):
1. Parcela (n=632; 191 con invasoras): A1 logística 500 m — OR urban_now=10.37 [1.44, 74.48], p=0.020; con habitat ajustado; OR urban_hist=0.02, p=0.005 (colinealidad urban_now–urban_hist r=0.72 → interpretación conjunta cautelosa). Modelo reducido (sin habitat): OR=1.74, p=0.44, pero gradiente crudo de terciles 0.086→0.227→0.652 → el efecto urbano está fuertemente mediado/confundido por el hábitat. Sensibilidad 50 m: no significativo (OR=1.53, p=0.57); 1000 m: OR=4.97, p=0.14 → efecto dependiente de la escala, máximo a 500 m.
2. A2 conteos condicionales (n=191, Poisson HC1): Gardening IRR=0.43 [0.19,0.97], p=0.043; Unintentional IRR=1.06, p=0.87; AgriForest IRR=1.21, p=0.87.
3. A3 composición por terciles de urbanización: Unintentional 54.1%→58.3%→66.7%; Gardening 37.8%→36.6%→31.6%; AgriForest 8.1%→5.1%→1.8%; chi2 global=9.65, p=0.047; par a par AgriForest low vs high p=0.017; Spearman(urban, fracción gardening) rho=-0.106, p=0.14.
4. Especie (n=81): vía × forma de crecimiento chi2=30.9, p=3.2e-6 (Gardening: 20/42 arbustos-árboles; Unintentional: 18/24 anuales). Éxito de invasión (OLS, SE agrupados por familia): Unintentional beta=+9.7, p=0.009; Perennial beta=-3.1, p=0.0001; log(mrt) beta=+2.3, p=0.03; R2=0.23. Nicho invadido mayor en Unintentional (0.75) que Gardening (0.45), KW p=0.047.
5. Temporal (Cataluña): Gardening pasa de 16.8% (antes de 1500) a 75.2% (1985-2019); AgriForest de 51.4% a 6.1%.
6. Diagnósticos: autocorrelación espacial de residuos logísticos despreciable (I≈0.0003, pares aleatorios <5 km); sobredispersión leve solo en n.unint (var 1.97 vs media 1.51); dummies de cambio 1956-2009 con |r|≤0.32 frente a coberturas (sin colinealidad severa; se reportan con cautela como pidió).

LIMITACIONES: (i) sin unión especie-parcela explícita, el efecto sobre "tipos" se infiere vía conteos por vía; (ii) el efecto urbano sobre presencia es dependiente de escala y en gran parte mediado por el hábitat — la afirmación sólida es la del cambio de composición; (iii) n.agfo escaso (23 conteos) limita potencia; (iv) OR del modelo completo con IC muy anchos (variable de cobertura 0-1); (v) filogenia no utilizable en este entorno (solo 77/81 tips emparejados; 4 duplicados con sufijo '2'); se usó familia como agrupación.

payload.hypothesis: Urban land use promotes the invasion of introduced plants mainly by filtering which plant types establish: invasion occurrence rises steeply with urbanization (8.6% of parcels with invaders in the lowest urban-cover tercile vs 65.2% in the highest, 500 m buffer), but this is largely mediated by habitat type (urban-habitat plots 83% invaded vs <7% in forests/scrub; habitat LRT p~1e-15). Within invaded plots, urbanization shifts composition of the invading flora: unintentionally introduced annual herbs with the broadest invaded niches increase their share (54%→67% from low to high urban tercile), while AgriForest introductions decline sharply (8%→2%, p=0.017) and gardening-introduced woody species decline mildly (38%→32%; gardening IRR=0.43, p=0.043). Overall invasion success is higher for unintentionally introduced species (+9.7 invaded plots vs gardening, p=0.009), species with broader invaded niche breadth (p=0.047) and longer residence time (p=0.03); and because the regional introduction pool is increasingly gardening-sourced (17% before 1500 → 75% in 1985-2019), the urban filter increasingly acts on an ornamental-dominated pool, favouring its ruderal, unintentionally-spread component.
payload.workflow: 1) Data inspection and sanity checks (dimensions, NAs, phylo tip matching 77/81, n.total=rowwise sum verified). 2) Plot-level (invaded_niche_pathways.csv, 632 plots): logistic GLM for presence of invaders with urban cover 2009/1956 + cropland 2009 (500 m main; 50 m and 1000 m sensitivity), covariates habitat/elevation/climate/distances; pathway-specific conditional Poisson GLMs (HC1) for n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo given n.total>0; composition of invaders across urbanization terciles with chi-square tests and Spearman trend; Moran-like residual autocorrelation check. 3) Species-level (invasion_success_pathways.csv, 81 species): pathway x growth.form cross-tab (chi-square), OLS of number of invaded plots on pathway x growth.form + log residence time + height with family-clustered SEs (phylogeny tools unavailable in environment), Kruskal-Wallis for niche breadth. 4) Temporal context from contingency table. 5) Supplementary: reduced models without habitat, overdispersion check, collinearity of land-change dummies, Urban-habitat-specific correlation. Tools: pandas 3.0.2, numpy, scipy 1.16.0, statsmodels 0.14.6.
payload.limitations: No explicit species-plot join (link via introduction pathway only); urban effect on occurrence is scale-dependent and largely habitat-mediated (solid claim is the compositional shift); n.agfo sparse (23 counts); wide CIs due to 0-1 cover scale; phylogeny not usable in this environment (family used as grouping; 4 duplicated tip labels unmatched).
